Subject: CuraSync pilot — strict routing exception and fallback hold request

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for running the pilot readiness call last week. As discussed with our compliance team, CuraSync requires the following for the initial production-like pilot (PHI subset):

- All inference must be processed within the US (no cross-region processing).
- No automatic fallback to cheaper/secondary model variants; we want a strict no-fallback policy for the pilot window.
- Auditable request and response logs for the pilot (retention 1 year), and evidence of KMS usage.

We understand this is operationally unusual. For timeline planning: we aim to start a 6-week pilot the week of 2028-06-12. Attached is our high-level security ask and an internal slide summarizing the risk drivers.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can support a strict no-fallback + US-only routing for this pilot, and what the expected operational gating items are? If there are mitigations (e.g., pinned model variant with identical weights but different quantization) that you can commit to, please call them out.

Appreciate a quick read — our CISO (cc) and Head of ML are looped.

Best,
Maria Gonzalez
CISO, CuraSync

Irene — quick ops read:

High-level: technically feasible but operationally heavyweight. Notes and risks: 

1) US-only routing: straightforward if we pin the pilot to a single region (us-west-2). We need explicit SLA on capacity; otherwise requests may queue during bursts.

2) No-fallback requirement: this is the bigger issue. Our serving layer currently uses graceful fallback to maintain latency SLOs — removing fallback increases the blast radius for model OOMs or GPU failures. For a 6-week pilot we can implement a strictly pinned variant and block automatic fallback, but we need:
   - Pre-warm capacity to match expected QPS + 30% headroom.
   - Runbook for manual failover (on-call escalation + a documented acceptance of potential downtime).

3) Auditable logs / KMS evidence: engineering can provide request/response logging and KMS usage traces but will require a short-lived retention policy override and a ticket to infra to ensure logs are exported to the customer-accessible audit bundle. That will take ~5 working days to validate.

Operational asks from us: a confirmed pilot traffic profile (expected concurency, avg tokens per request), an acceptance of possible manual failover windows, and a signed security exception acknowledging reduced automatic fallback.

If product is OK with the manual failover plan and Legal signs off on exception language, Ops can greenlight. 

—Marcus

Thanks Marcus — this tracks. Product thoughts / suggested mitigation: 

1) Pinned variant: we can onboard a pinned model binary (same weights) that is guaranteed not to route to any fallback variants. That meets their "no-fallback" ask at the model-selection level rather than nuking runtime fallback globally.

2) Canary cohort + manual rollback: run the pilot on a 10% cohort for week 1 with full sanity checks (latency, error rate, token cost). If stable, expand to 100% for weeks 2–6. During week 1 we keep manual failover only (no automatic fallback). That reduces risk while honoring the pilot constraints.

3) Audit & runbook: Product will own the acceptance criteria doc and a short risk-acknowledgement template for Legal to sign. Ops to produce the audit bundle. We need CS to collect expected QPS and sample prompts.

4) Timeline: if Ops can validate logging & KMS traces in 5 business days, and Legal signs the exception doc, we can still hit the week-of-2028-06-12 start for a controlled pilot.

Action items I propose now:
- Dev / Marcus: confirm pre-warm cost estimate and whether pre-warm can be scheduled without impacting other customers (reply by EOD).
- Lauren / CS: get pilot traffic profile + list of example prompts (tomorrow).
- Irene: draft the exception language for Legal and share with Maria for her review.

Irene — happy to jump on a short sync with Ops if helpful. This approach preserves CuraSync's security posture while keeping our operational controls intact.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Group PM, Inference Platform
